gap: The attestation strip makes an absolute claim over a set that is only the reader's own. Measured on an isolated instance on 8086 against a copy of this repository's own stores, day 2026-08-07, four real sessions: GET /api/history/since answers scope all, changed 77, attempted 108, refused 31, verdict changed for an admin, and scope self, changed 0, attempted 0, refused 0, verdict unchanged for a plain operator, over the same store in the same second. The surface then prints the unqualified sentence, read from the page in Hebrew: 'shum davar lo hishtana meaz oto yom' (Nothing has changed since that day), with no scope word anywhere on the strip. The only scope statement on the destination is the footer line 'mutzagim hashinuyim shelachem vechol nekudot hashichzur', measured at 859 px below the bottom of the strip and outside a 941 px viewport on landing, so it is not on screen when the claim is read. This is the seventh route of the defect class rounds 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 closed, taken in the one dimension none of them checked: the reader's own permission scope. HistorySince.jsx line 113 chooses the empty sentence from changeCount alone and never reads body.scope, which the endpoint already emits beside it, the same key history_api_reach already publishes as in_scope and scope for the footer. The file's own comment at lines 74 to 78 states the rule it breaks: printing a figure the record cannot support in the one sentence a compliance owner reads first is a false attestation. A compliance_owner job on a role operator account is reachable today, and specification section 2.1 says job never decides permission, so this reader exists. The fix is inside this piece's own files: read body.scope on the strip, qualify both the count sentence and the empty sentence in both languages, and pin it with a test that builds one store, reads it as an admin and as an operator, and asserts the two sentences cannot both be absolute.
